Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation and helpful context on your goals for customer support automation. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the proposed 4-week POC approach and next steps so we have alignment on success criteria, ownership, and how we’ll evaluate model quality (offline evals vs online shadow).

High-level POC plan (proposed):
- Week 0 (prep): data sampling & access, onboarding to a redwood dev account, confirm required security controls.
- Week 1: baseline run (your current model or rules) + initial Redwood model mapping and small-scale offline evals.
- Week 2: integrate Redwood API into a shadow/test route (online shadow) capturing predictions and telemetry.
- Week 3: refine prompts/params, run comparison experiments, start user acceptance sampling with internal reviewers.
- Week 4: final evaluation, success review, and decision on next steps (expand to production/dedicated).

POC owners:
- Acme: Samir (Product Lead), Priya (Engineering).
- Redwood: Rachel (AE, overall POC), Vivek (SE, integration & evals), Marissa (CS, onboarding & ops).

Success criteria (draft) — see attached acme_poc_success_criteria.pdf:
- Accuracy: >= 85% pass rate on resolved customer intent classification (measured on a labeled holdout).
- Latency: 95th percentile tail <= 800ms for typical query size (as measured in the shadow route).
- Safety/hallucination: < 2% hallucination rate on a 500-sample audit set.
- Business KPI: median handle-time reduction >= 12% across sampled tickets (optional).

Evals methodology — quick notes:
- Offline evals: run on labeled datasets you provide. Good for repeatable metric comparisons and iteration (precision/recall, hallucination audits).
- Online shadow: runs the model in parallel with prod, capturing real requests/outputs and real latency. Useful for live performance and integration regression checks.
- Grading rubric: we propose a combined pass/fail score with weighted metrics (40% correctness, 30% hallucination/safety, 20% latency, 10% business KPI). Detailed sheet attached (evaluation_rubric.xlsx).

Next steps (please confirm):
1) You share a ~500-example labeled holdout + 2k unlabeled sample by end of this week.
2) Redwood sends onboarding access + initial scripts for offline evals by Tue 2/24.
3) Schedule a 30-min tech sync (Vivek + Priya + Alex) to finalize shadow routing requirements — suggested Tue 2/24 10:00am PT.

If that overall approach looks good, I’ll send a short MAM (mutual action plan) with these milestones and owners.

Thanks —

Hi Samir / team — quick answers inline and a few notes on the eval rubric: 

1) Stratified sample: yes — that's the right approach. Please include labels for ticket_type so we can compute per-class metrics. We recommend at least ~50 examples per low-volume class to get stable estimates.

2) Hallucination definition: for this POC we define a hallucination as any model-generated assertion that is factually incorrect OR introduces an unsupported claim that could mislead a customer (e.g., "Your plan includes X" when account data doesn't show it). Missing citation is NOT automatically a hallucination unless the response asserts a verifiable but incorrect fact. We'll include a short checklist in the rubric to help raters mark borderline cases.

3) PII/redaction and logging: Redwood will provide a client-side middleware snippet to redacted sensitive fields before they leave Acme's environment; logs captured in the shadow route will be stored in an encrypted Redshift export with access limited to named owners. We'll document retention and access controls in the onboarding notes.

Evals approach recommendation:
- Start with offline evals to tune prompts and measure baseline metrics on the labeled holdout. This helps set thresholds (e.g., >=85% accuracy).
- Then run a 7–10 day online shadow to validate latency and real-world behavior. Use the same scoring rubric so we can compare offline-to-online drift.
- Raters: combination of Acme SMEs + Redwood QA engineers for initial 200-case audit (blinded). Afterward we can hand off to Acme-only raters if you prefer.

Grading rubric highlights (see evaluation_rubric.xlsx):
- Correctness (0–2): 0 incorrect, 1 partially correct, 2 fully correct.
- Hallucination flag (yes/no). Any yes sets the item to fail regardless of correctness score in safety-critical classes.
- Latency bucket labels: <200ms / 200–500ms / 500–800ms / >800ms. Pass if 95th <= 800ms.
- Composite score = (Correctness_score / 2)*0.4 + (1 - Hallucination_rate)*0.3 + latency_score*0.2 + business_kpi_score*0.1 (sheet has the mapping).

I'll upload a short example script and the rubric to the Drive folder tonight. For the integration window, Priya / Alex — happy to take the 2-hour slot you propose; let Rachel and I know the exact times and I'll ensure we're available.

Thanks —
Vivek
